title: Foundations Checkpoint
description: Compare arrays and linked lists for indexed access, insertion, and deletion. Give the time complexity of each operation and explain one practical tradeoff. Submit your explanation as text.

title: Concept Practice
description: Write pseudocode for a stack and a queue. Trace both structures through five operations and explain how underflow is handled. Submit the pseudocode and trace as text.

title: Mini Project
description: Design a binary search tree with insert and search operations. Submit pseudocode, example inputs and outputs, and an analysis of balanced versus worst-case performance.

title: Analysis & Reflection
description: Compare breadth-first and depth-first traversal on a small graph. Show the visit order, explain your choice of data structure, and discuss when each traversal is useful.

title: Applied Challenge
description: Propose a hash-table design for a contact directory. Explain hashing, collision handling, resizing, and expected lookup cost. Include three edge cases and their expected behavior.

title: Final Synthesis
description: Design a route-planning solution using graphs. Submit pseudocode, a worked example, complexity analysis, and a justification of the algorithm and data structures you selected.

title: Foundations Checkpoint
description: Write semantic HTML for a course page with navigation, headings, and an assignment form. Explain the accessible name and label of each interactive element.

title: Concept Practice
description: Submit CSS for a responsive two-column layout that collapses on small screens. Explain keyboard focus styles, contrast choices, and how long content is handled.

title: Mini Project
description: Write a typed React component for a course card and a filtered course list. Submit the component code as text and explain props, stable keys, and empty states.

title: Analysis & Reflection
description: Review a form workflow for validation, error recovery, and accessibility. Describe three failure cases and propose specific changes, including how success is announced.

title: Applied Challenge
description: Design a routed student dashboard with shared state. Submit a route map, TypeScript state model, and pseudocode for preventing access to another student's work.

title: Final Synthesis
description: Submit a technical design for an accessible learning app. Cover component boundaries, state updates, validation, responsive behavior, and a manual verification checklist.

title: Foundations Checkpoint
description: Describe the variables and units in a fictional student-performance dataset. Identify numeric and categorical fields and explain why correlation does not establish causation.

title: Concept Practice
description: Propose a cleaning plan for missing values, duplicate records, and inconsistent date formats. Include a before-and-after example and justify which records should be retained.

title: Mini Project
description: Provide an exploratory analysis of a small fictional dataset. Submit summary statistics, descriptions of two appropriate charts, and limitations of the sample.

title: Analysis & Reflection
description: Evaluate a reported relationship between submission timing and grades. Discuss selection bias, confounding factors, sample size, and what the evidence cannot establish.

title: Applied Challenge
description: Design a train-validation-test split for a prediction task. Explain leakage prevention, baseline performance, and the evaluation metric you would use.

title: Final Synthesis
description: Write an analysis brief covering data preparation, exploratory findings, model evaluation, and limitations. Distinguish measured results from hypotheses and recommendations.

title: Foundations Checkpoint
description: Frame a usability problem for a fictional campus service. Identify the users, their task, current obstacles, and a measurable success criterion without assuming a solution.

title: Concept Practice
description: Create five non-leading interview questions and a consent introduction. Explain how you would recruit participants and protect their privacy.

title: Mini Project
description: Describe a low-fidelity prototype for the campus service. Submit a screen-by-screen flow, key interactions, and how errors and empty states are communicated.

title: Analysis & Reflection
description: Critique your prototype against usability and accessibility principles. Explain three design tradeoffs and separate user evidence from your own assumptions.

title: Applied Challenge
description: Write a usability-test plan with three tasks, observation criteria, and a way to measure task success. Explain how you would avoid coaching participants.

title: Final Synthesis
description: Write a product-design case study connecting the problem, research, prototype, evaluation, and revisions. Include remaining accessibility concerns and next steps.
